name: Gridline Street Vendor's Weather Layering Set
description:
A practical, self-curated layering kit worn by Circuit-level street food vendors, market stall operators, and mobile cart workers who spend full shifts exposed to M88's variable weather — acid-rain squalls, thermal inversions, and the cold lake-corridor wind that scours the elevated walkways. The outermost layer is a waist-length anorak in weatherproof sage-green synth-wax, hood cinched with a toggle drawstring, chest pocket sealed with a magnetic flap. A small embroidered patch on the left shoulder reads the vendor's licensed stall number in Circuit's market registry — required by city ordinance, often accompanied by a handmade decorative border the vendor has added themselves. Beneath the anorak, a heavy-duty apron in charcoal canvas covers the torso from collar to knee, cross-back straps distributing the weight of deep front pockets loaded with tools, condiment packets, a card reader, and small wares. The apron's bib has a transparent ID-sleeve pocket for the vendor's Circuit commerce license. Under the apron, a rust-orange thermal mid-layer pullover with a funnel neck provides insulation. Trousers are dark olive cargo-cut synth-twill, knee-reinforced for the crouching and kneeling of restocking and equipment maintenance. Footwear is a pair of Ashgrove Linework Work Boots — oil-resistant flat sole, composite toe, ankle-height.

This isn't a uniform — it's an ecosystem of practical choices refined over seasons. Vendors working gene-compatible builds often have their apron straps widened or the anorak hood enlarged to accommodate horns or enhanced ear structures; most of these modifications are hand-sewn. The stall number patch is the only branding required, but vendors frequently add layers of personal expression: painted apron pockets, lucky charms clipped to the anorak zipper pull, an ancestor's recipe card laminated and tucked behind the ID sleeve.
functionality: Full weather protection via layering system, deep-pocket apron for vendor tools and wares, commerce license ID sleeve, oil-resistant composite-toe footwear, knee reinforcement for restocking work, adjustable hood for weather and gene-modification accommodation
what_it_says: Self-employed, licensed, and proud of it. The stall number patch signals legitimacy in a city that aggressively culls unlicensed vendors. The personal touches say this person has been doing this long enough to make it their own.
manufacturer: Self-assembled; anorak from Gridline Outerwear (street brand), apron from Driftmarket Canvas Supply, boots from Ashgrove
story_hooks: A vendor's stall number patch is registered to a person who died eighteen months ago — someone has been operating under a dead person's license, and the market registry is finally running audits.
The laminated recipe card behind a vendor's ID sleeve is written in a language no translator module recognizes — and a customer with an unusual background suddenly goes very still when they see it.

A Circuit vendor's cart is the only establishment on a particular elevated walkway that stays open during a corponation-enforced curfew — they know something about why, and the apron pockets hold more than condiments.
